title: CONSISTENT HASHING
subtitle: Add or remove a node and move only a small share of the keys.
footer: System Design, Step by Step · core concepts

items: Nodes and keys hash onto a ring.
A key belongs to the next node clockwise.
Adding a node moves only the keys in one arc (~1/N), unlike hash % N which moves almost everything. Virtual nodes even out the load.

blocks.text: Distributed caches, Cassandra, DynamoDB, L7 routing of video/doc IDs to servers.

items: Place nodes and keys on the same hash ring.
A key belongs to the first node clockwise from it.
Use virtual nodes (many points per server) to even out load.
Adding a node moves roughly 1/N of keys; hash % N moves almost all of them.

blocks.text: "Cache nodes sit on a consistent-hash ring with virtual nodes, so adding a node remaps about 1/N of keys instead of emptying the whole cache."
